A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARCQuant research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, nine figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, perplexity, coding and mathematics evaluations, calibration studies, and GPU latency and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MicroMix comparisons, vLLM generation measurements, and evaluations of Llama 3.1-70B and Mixtral 8x7B-Instruct.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D retain the same channel selection, residual quantization, weight duplication, fused kernel, and unified GEMM procedure. The reported vLLM integration does not introduce a documented change to the quantization algorithm.

E1.justification: Efficiency coverage expands from kernel execution and prefill to autoregressive generation and decoding in vLLM (new Table 4). The calibration datasets and accuracy-evaluation domains remain unchanged; the additional model sizes and architectures are configuration changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated MicroMix rows for all three existing models while retaining every previous comparator. New Table 4 compares generation throughput against FP16 and FP8. MicroMix was previously discussed only as related work.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct vLLM generation protocol measuring total and decoding throughput on Qwen2.5-7B: RTX 5090, batch size 8, generation length 128, and context lengths 1024 and 2048. It also adds 70B dense and Mixtral MoE configurations; Table 9 averages four zero-shot tasks, whereas Table 1 averages five. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an explicit scalability check asking whether ARCQuant remains effective on substantially larger dense models and sparse MoE architectures, supported by Table 9 comparisons against RTN and FP16. Existing calibration-sensitivity and quantization-format studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0 in Appendix C. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Existing scores remain unchanged, but v2 substantially extends the reported evidence with MicroMix results and Tables 4 and 9. Table 4 reports ARCQuant decoding throughput of 2342 and 1249 tokens/s versus FP16's 1195 and 600. Table 9 reports Llama 3.1-70B perplexity of 3.62 versus RTN's 3.85. Mixtral improves on aggregate metrics, although its HellaSwag accuracy is 84.94 versus RTN's 85.09.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, assumptions, equations, and NVFP4-versus-MXFP8 error-bound derivation in Section 3.4 are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same numerical-format definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified NVFP4 computation, residual compensation, MXFP8-comparable error bounds, accuracy, and hardware efficiency. The new experiments provide additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: New passages interpret the added experiments as evidence that efficiency extends to decoding and that accuracy generalizes to larger dense and MoE models. Appendix D now distinguishes completed vLLM benchmarking integration from future full serving support. The existing weight-quantization, hardware, and offline-calibration limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly states that calibration artifacts are provided in supplementary material. v2 also documents MicroMix's mixed-precision configuration and the new vLLM benchmark settings, and updates the deployment status in Appendix D. The repository address, software versions, calibration settings, and kernel implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. FlatQuant's reference changes from its 2024 preprint to its ICML 2025 publication, representing the same work. MicroMix was already cited and discussed in v1.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the baseline description, adds paragraphs explaining the new experiments, updates reproducibility and future-work prose, and adds acknowledgments. Minor punctuation and bibliographic edits accompany these changes; the overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 with MicroMix rows and adds the generation-throughput and larger-model tables. Existing appendix tables are renumbered, Figure 8 moves within the page layout, and surrounding text reflows. All nine existing figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The MicroMix comparison, actual vLLM decoding measurements, and 70B/MoE evaluations strengthen empirical support for ARCQuant's practical efficiency and generality beyond v1's evidence. These are useful, targeted improvements. Deployment validation remains limited to one model and GPU for generation, full serving support is still future work, and the Mixtral results require qualification rather than a claim of improvement on every metric.
